note: Shapes a dive uses: the-zoom-in and levels (layer by layer down), reveal (the deepest point), countdown (depth counting), question-chain.

shapes.name: Levels
shapes.when: only when the topic IS a ladder people wait to climb: levels of wealth, $100 to a strap to a pallet to a room, an hour to a decade
shapes.beats: hook -> promise the ladder ('four steps up') -> each level a beat, the counter climbing -> the turn at the top -> the payoff

shapes.name: The reveal (open loop and clues)
shapes.when: how a business really makes money, a secret of the rich, a billionaire question: there is one hidden answer
shapes.beats: hook: the surprising fact and the question, no answer -> promise ('here's how') -> clue one, clue two, clue three, each a bigger piece -> the turn (the piece nobody expects) -> the payoff answers the hook in one line

reference.title: Why does the casino always win, even when nobody cheats? | How Casinos Make Money

shapes.name: Countdown
shapes.when: a handful of things of one kind (tricks, traps, ways): number three, two, then the biggest
shapes.beats: hook: the biggest one teased, not shown -> promise ('three ways, the last is the worst') -> three, two -> the turn -> number one, the payoff

reference.title: 6 Ways Rich People Make Money With Debt

shapes.name: The question chain (asker and explainer)
shapes.when: a billionaire or big-money mechanism with several layers: how the rich pay no tax, how a company really earns, why a famous person does something strange
shapes.beats: hook: the asker states the shocking fact and asks why -> the explainer answers in one line and one picture -> the asker's next, sharper question (doubt, then how, then a real example, then outrage, then 'and people like us?') -> each answer a real name and a figure, a named term on a card -> the named secret -> a 3-line recap, the lesson, the asker's last question to the viewer

reference.title: Why Billionaires Take $0 Salary… But Never Go Broke

shapes.name: The zoom-in
shapes.when: a famous total too big to picture, made real by dividing it down to one night and one person; fits tours, stadiums, launches, sales days
shapes.beats: hook: the giant total with the famous name, as one striking rate -> promise: how can it be that much? -> how the money is really made, one step a beat (who pays, for what, the rule behind it) -> the turn: the part people miss (what the total is NOT, or who really pays) -> payoff: the most surprising slice, and a question. One time rate at most: never the same total per hour, per day, per year
